name: What Data Cannot Tell You
title: What Data Cannot Tell You
answer: Data only captures part of a student's life and learning, so decisions about students should combine data with what adults know from knowing the student. Districts should resist treating what is measurable as all that matters, because a data system that crowds out attention to hard-to-measure goals does harm even when every number is accurate. Data should serve the mission of education, not define it.

crumbs.name: Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System

sections.body: This idea holds that data captures only part of a student's life and learning. A test score does not show curiosity, kindness, creativity, or resilience, and attendance data does not show why a student missed school. Teachers see much that no system records. The problem it solves is the temptation to treat what is measurable as all that matters, which can crowd out attention to the most important goals of education. Decisions about students should therefore combine data with what adults know from knowing the student.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, decisions about students combine data with what adults know from knowing the student. A student whose scores dipped may be dealing with a family crisis, and a student with average scores may have made remarkable growth from a hard start. The full picture requires people, so teachers and leaders bring their own knowledge of the student alongside any numbers. Districts should resist the temptation to treat what is measurable as all that matters. The text does not give grade band examples.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or finding for this idea. It rests on practice and on the judgement that some of the most important goals of education are hard to measure. The book's own claim is that a data system which crowds out attention to those goals does harm even when every number is accurate. No evidence label is stated in the supplied text.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits are that data captures only part of a student's life and learning, and that some of the most important goals of education are hard to measure. The risk is a data system that crowds out attention to those goals, which does harm even when every number is accurate. The decisions that stay with a person are the judgements about students that combine data with what adults know from knowing the student. Districts should resist treating what is measurable as all that matters, and data should serve the mission, not define it.
